title: GTA VI preorders: announced prices, editions and the download-code detail
shortdescription: Rockstar’s June 2026 announcement listed two console editions and a boxed download code. Platform, storage, refund terms and local pricing belong in the purchase decision.
description:
Rockstar said preorders would begin June 25 at midnight local time, with a November 19, 2026 launch planned for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Its U.S. announcement listed the standard game at $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition at $99.99.

The release also said digital preloading would begin November 12 and described the physical version as a box containing a download code. That distinction matters to buyers expecting a playable disc or a conventional second-hand purchase.

Confirm the platform, region, edition contents and local price at the official store. Read cancellation and refund terms before redeeming or downloading anything. The announcement’s release date is a publisher commitment, not evidence that the game has already shipped.

The launch notice did not announce a PC edition. Avoid treating an unofficial PC preorder listing as confirmation. Bonus items and subscription trials should be assessed separately from the game’s price, including whether a trial renews. This guide reports announced terms; it is not a review of the finished game.

title: Disney estimates a $160 million domestic opening for Toy Story 5
shortdescription: Disney estimated a $312 million worldwide opening for Toy Story 5 in June 2026. Territory, release window and exhibition shares explain what that gross measures.
description:
Disney said Toy Story 5 opened to an estimated $160 million domestically and $152 million overseas, for $312 million worldwide. Its June 21 announcement described the result as the franchise’s largest opening across those measures.

The company also called it the second-largest domestic animated opening, behind Incredibles 2. The comparison should retain its territory, time window and estimate status; ‘record opening’ without those qualifications is ambiguous.

A theatrical gross is ticket revenue before the division between exhibitors and distributors. It is not the studio’s profit, and opening-weekend sales do not establish how the film will perform over its full run.

A useful follow-up compares finalized weekend figures, later attendance and the number of markets in release. Inflation, premium formats and ticket prices also complicate comparisons with older films. Disney is both the source of these estimates and the company promoting the release, so its celebratory interpretation is kept separate from the reported figures.

title: Wenders and Kinski announce resolution over disputed Wrong Move scene
shortdescription: A July 2026 joint statement said the disputed scene had been removed at Kinski’s request. Distribution of updated versions was a separate practical question.
description:
The Wim Wenders Foundation’s June 3 statement said Wrong Move would be withdrawn from distribution and public exhibition following concerns raised by Nastassja Kinski about a scene filmed when she was 13. Wenders acknowledged that she should have been better protected and apologized.

On July 23, he said the scene would be removed from the film. A July 30 joint statement said the differences had been resolved and that he had complied with Kinski’s request to make the cut.

An agreement about an edit does not establish when every distributor will replace a version or restore access. Readers seeking the film should check the rights holder’s current distribution information.

The case also raises a wider question for film archives: how to preserve a historical record while responding to the experience of someone depicted as a child. That debate can be reported without recirculating the material that prompted the complaint. The statements are the basis for this update, not an independent judgment about every historical circumstance.

title: DC Studios Overhaul: Skydance Ousts James Gunn and Peter Safran, Taps Former Marvel Executive Jeremy Latcham to Lead
seoTitle: DC Studios Leadership Shake-Up: Skydance Replaces Gunn & Safran With Marvel Veteran Jeremy Latcham | Entertainment News
shortdescription: In a sweeping post-acquisition restructuring, Skydance has ended the co-CEO tenure of James Gunn and Peter Safran at DC Studios, installing veteran former Marvel Studios producer Jeremy Latcham to spearhead the franchise's next era.
metaDescription: Skydance is shaking up DC Studios once again, replacing co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran with veteran Marvel Studios producer Jeremy Latcham. Explore what the leadership transition means for the DC Universe slate.
description:
DC Studios is undergoing another major leadership overhaul. Following its corporate consolidation, Skydance has parted ways with DC Studios co-chairmen and chief executive officers James Gunn and Peter Safran, appointing veteran film producer and former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham to take charge of the comic-book division.

Gunn and Safran were originally appointed in late 2022 to unify DC's film, television and animation output under a multi-year blueprint titled 'Chapter One: Gods and Monsters.' While their tenure saw the launch of key projects aimed at resetting the franchise's creative continuity, new parent leadership at Skydance opted to install its own executive architecture to oversee the intellectual property moving forward.

Jeremy Latcham brings more than a decade of high-level franchise production experience from Marvel Studios, where he served as an executive producer on foundational Infinity Saga blockbusters including The Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy, Avengers: Age of Ultron and Spider-Man: Homecoming. After leaving Marvel in 2017, Latcham transitioned into major studio producing deals, including collaborating on big-budget ensemble features such as Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves.

An executive change at the top of a studio does not automatically cancel every project currently in production or post-production. Separate between films that have already completed principal photography, projects in active pre-production with committed talent contracts, and unproduced development titles that were only announced as part of an earlier slate. Incoming studio heads routinely audit development pipelines while allowing near-complete theatrical releases to proceed.

Industry observers and audiences should look next for formal studio communications clarifying Latcham's exact reporting line, whether DC Studios will retain a single-executive structure rather than the dual creative-and-business model shared by Gunn and Safran, and which upcoming theatrical and streaming titles remain on the release calendar.

sections.heading: A New Regime at DC Studios
paragraphs: DC Studios is undergoing another major leadership overhaul. Following its corporate consolidation, Skydance has parted ways with DC Studios co-chairmen and chief executive officers James Gunn and Peter Safran, appointing veteran film producer and former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham to take charge of the comic-book division.

The move marks a decisive effort by Skydance leadership to install its own executive architecture atop one of Hollywood's most valuable—and historically turbulent—intellectual property libraries. Rather than maintaining the dual creative-and-executive partnership that defined the previous four years, Skydance has turned to a seasoned production veteran with deep roots in rival Marvel's most commercially stable era.

sections.heading: The End of the Gunn and Safran Era
paragraphs: Gunn and Safran were hired in late 2022 to bring cohesion to DC's fractured film, television, and animation pipelines. Tasked with building an interconnected canon across theatrical features and streaming series, the duo unveiled 'Chapter One: Gods and Monsters' in early 2023 and oversaw the creative reset anchored by Superman.

Despite the pair's mandate to establish a decade-long narrative arc, corporate ownership transitions in Hollywood frequently trigger changes at the division-head level. Incoming parent companies often prefer executives aligned with their own capital allocation frameworks, production budgets, and theatrical windowing strategies.

sections.heading: Who Is Jeremy Latcham?
paragraphs: Jeremy Latcham brings more than a decade of high-level franchise production experience from Marvel Studios, where he rose to Senior Vice President of Production and Development during the formative years of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. During his tenure, he was credited as an executive producer on foundational Infinity Saga blockbusters including The Avengers (2012), Guardians of the Galaxy (2014)—notably collaborating with Gunn—Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015), and Spider-Man: Homecoming (2017).

After departing Marvel in 2017 to launch his own production banner, Latcham produced Bad Times at the El Royale and the critically praised ensemble fantasy feature Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves (2023) for Paramount and eOne. His track record blending large-scale visual effects management with character-driven ensemble storytelling made him a natural fit for Skydance's production-first ethos.

sections.heading: How to Evaluate the Impact on the DC Slate
paragraphs: An executive change at the top of a studio does not automatically cancel every project currently in the pipeline. Readers and industry analysts should distinguish between three distinct tiers of production: completed or nearly completed projects in post-production, greenlit projects with binding pay-or-play talent commitments, and early development titles that existed primarily as slate announcements.

Incoming studio leadership routinely audits unproduced development slates to align budgets and tone with the parent company's financial targets, while allowing completed films and series to proceed through their theatrical and streaming release windows. Until DC Studios issues an updated production calendar under Latcham, claims that the entire existing canon has been scrapped or retained wholesale should be treated with caution.
